entries.stanceLine: Breakouts suspect in both directions today — The obvious draw (PDL 10433.8) sits beyond what's left of a typical day's range — targets past it are stretch-only today.

signals.text: The obvious draw (PDL 10433.8) sits beyond what's left of a typical day's range — targets past it are stretch-only today.
Sterling is at the 89th percentile of its 20-day range and still rising — a persistent FX headwind capping upside breaks (weak GBP is what lifts FTSE).
UK CPI @ 07:00 BST today — pre-release breaks are positioning, not conviction.
GBP is a crowded short — a short-squeeze higher in sterling is a latent slap for upside breaks (strong GBP weighs on FTSE).

entries.aiStanceLine: Due to UK CPI already having fired at 07:00 BST, 56% of the 14-day average daily range consumed within the first ten minutes, and sterling pinned at the 89th percentile of its 20-day range, the ORB break higher looks like an event-flush rather than a conviction trend day — fade risk is elevated.
aiBullets: The gap of +35.4 pts consumed ~25% of the 140.2-pt ADR before a single ORB candle closed — combining that with the 56% ADR-used figure means roughly 60 pts of typical range remains for the full session, making extended trend targets thin.

Brent +1.89% is the only sector-level tailwind with real index weight (Shell + BP are top-5 members); copper flat and banks neutral means energy alone is carrying the bull case — a single-sector rally rarely sustains a full ORB trend day.

GBP COT [Commitment of Traders, a report showing how large funds are positioned] shows net short of -72,474 contracts but with +17,517 added long in the last week — shorts are already covering, so a further sterling squeeze higher (which would be a FTSE headwind) is a live risk that the mechanical signals flag individually but the combination with a post-CPI gap makes particularly dangerous for long ORB runners.

Prior week high (10616.2) and overnight high (10613.6) sit within 3 points of each other just above current price (10630.1 at snapshot) — this double-resistance confluence directly above the ORB break level raises the probability of a stall or reversal rather than clean extension.
